Creative Analysis

🇧🇪

Belgium

25 ads · €5031 spend · 185 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Carousel format dominates: 'Carousel_120237873305580396 - Copy' drives 78 purchases at 9.01x ROAS — it's eating 30% of budget and delivering the bulk of volume.
• Product-specific statics are efficiency monsters: 'Static _ Diamond Earstud #4' at 18.32x ROAS and €8.37 CPP is the best ad in the account, and 'Static _ Edge #1' at 7.61x confirms single-product hero shots convert hard in Belgium.
• UGC has upside when done right: 'Static _ UGC #1' (6.7x) and 'Static _ UGC #4' (4.99x) prove the format works — the problem is consistency, not the concept.
❌ What's Not Working
• Partner creatives are an expensive gamble: 'Static _ Partner #3' burned €70 for 1 purchase (1.14x ROAS), 'Static _ Partner #4' has a €79.44 CPP despite high CTR — clicks without conversions means wrong audience or weak landing.
• Half the UGC variants are duds: 'Static _ UGC #3' (1.45x, €62 CPP) and 'Static _ UGC #2' (2.05x, €45 CPP) drag down the format's average — suggesting not all UGC creators or angles are equal.
• Heart collection has zero proof of concept: three Heart ads ('Heart Catalog #1', 'Heart Tag #1', 'Heart White #1') have combined €49 spend and zero purchases — Meta isn't finding buyers for this product/angle.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product hero statics with single bestselling SKUs — Diamond Earstud and Edge prove that isolating one hero product with clean creative crushes it in Belgium. Build 3-4 new variants per winning SKU.
• Carousel format iterations — the only carousel is the top spender and top performer. Create carousels for Diamond Earstud, Edge, and Heart Tag collections. This format is criminally under-explored.
• Video Creative series expansion — 'Video _ Creative #3' (5.69x) and '#2' (2.86x at scale) show video storytelling converts. Produce #4 and #5 with the same production style but new products or angles.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause 'Static _ Partner #3' and 'Static _ UGC #3' immediately — sub-1.5x ROAS with enough spend to confirm they're losers.
• Stop duplicating mediocre ads: 'Video _ Creative #2 - Copy' is a worse version of the original (2.26x vs 2.86x) eating €113 for 3 purchases. Duplication is not a strategy.
• Deprioritize Partner creative production — 4 Partner ads averaging 2.34x ROAS and €56.59 CPP is the worst-performing format in the account. Reallocate that creator budget to UGC or product shoots.

Germany

5 ads · €1071 spend · 8 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Video format drives every single purchase in DE — both 'Video _ Stack #1' (6 purch.) and 'Video _ Kay #1' (2 purch.) convert while statics sit at zero.
• Stack concept generates the most volume (6 purchases on €684) showing the stacking/layering story resonates with German audiences.
• Earstud content pulls the highest engagement — 'Video _ Earstud New #1' hit 344% CTR on minimal spend, signaling strong thumb-stop potential.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero ads are profitable in Germany — the best ROAS is a measly 1.36x ('Video _ Kay #1'). The entire market is underwater.
• Static creative is dead on arrival — 'Static _ Earstud New #1' burned €130 with zero purchases. No static has converted.
• CPP of €114-121 is absurdly high for an affordable luxury brand. The funnel leaks hard post-click, suggesting landing page or offer mismatch for the DE audience.
⬆ Double Down On
• Video-first creative only for DE — every conversion came from video. Produce 3-4 new video variants of Stack and Kay with tighter hooks and German-market messaging.
• Earstud video content — the 344% CTR on 'Video _ Earstud New #1' is a screaming engagement signal that never got budget. Give it room to prove purchase intent.
• Introduce UGC to Germany — there is literally zero UGC running. German consumers over-index on authenticity and peer validation; this is a massive gap.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• 'Static _ Earstud New #1' — €130, zero purchases, zero signal. Dead.
• Static format in DE entirely — not a single static converted. Stop allocating budget to stills in this market until a UGC-style static proves otherwise.
• Stop running current creatives at these CPPs without landing page or offer changes — you're funding Meta, not revenue.

Kamping Kitsch Club — Ads Report

5 August 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €2861 spend · 308 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Static creative is the undisputed winner: 12 of 13 converting ads are static. 'Static _ Berekening #2' delivers 44.15x ROAS at €3.67 CPP — the best unit economics in the account.
• Price-math and discount-code framing crushes: 'Static _ Code #1' variants average ~25x ROAS across both instances, and 'Goedkoopste' (cheapest) converts at 13x. Rational value messaging outperforms emotional.
• Artist-name callouts drive purchase intent: 'Static _ RUBEN' hits 19.27x ROAS with 38 purchases at €7.44 CPP — naming a specific artist in static creative converts far better than generic lineup teasers.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video creative is a conversion black hole: 'Video _ Aftermovie #1' burned €144 for 2 purchases at €72.24 CPP (1.26x ROAS). 'Video _ McDrummer Steen' and 'Video _ McDrummer Vrijgezelle' spent €71 combined with zero purchases. The video-first assumption is wrong for this account.
• Sky-high CTR with zero conversions = vanity: 'Static _ Organic #1' (1331% CTR, 0 purchases) and McDrummer videos (900–1150% CTR, 0 purchases) prove engagement bait doesn't sell tickets.
• 'Waar vo' original underperforms its copy: 'Static _ Waar vo #1' at 3.66x ROAS and €29.76 CPP vs its copy variant at 8.39x — the original ad is dragging down the concept.
⬆ Double Down On
• More price-math/value-calculation statics: 'Berekening' is the #1 ROAS concept in the entire account (44x). Produce 3+ new variants with different cost-per-hour, cost-vs-alternatives, or savings angles.
• Artist-specific static ads for every confirmed headliner: 'RUBEN' proves the format. Roll out individual statics per artist name with ticket CTA — this is a repeatable template.
• Discount code urgency statics: Both 'Code #1' instances outperform at 16–33x ROAS. Create new code variants with expiry countdowns, limited-quantity framing, and group-deal angles.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the aftermovie as a conversion ad immediately. At €72 CPP it costs 9x the account average. Use it for reach/awareness only, never in purchase-optimized campaigns.
• Kill McDrummer video series from conversion campaigns. Three variants tested, two with zero purchases. Entertaining content ≠ ticket sales. Stop spending on engagement metrics.
• Kill 'Static _ Organic #1' — if it can't convert at any spend level with 1331% CTR, the landing experience or audience match is fundamentally broken.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €13361 spend · 286 leads
✅ What's Working
• Comparison ('Vergelijking') creatives are the undisputed engine — 5 of the top 7 CPL performers use this angle. 'Static _ Vergelijking #1 - Copy' delivers a stunning €25.31 CPL at scale (24 leads on €608).
• 'General Video #1' proves video can compete with statics, pulling €38.44 CPL with 21 leads — the only video format with real traction.
• The highest-spend ad 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy' is a reliable workhorse: 97 leads at €43.17 CPL, showing the comparison frame has legs at volume.
❌ What's Not Working
• Poll and De Tijd angles are money pits — 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy 2' at €69.45 CPL and 'Static _ De Tijd 2' at €60.12 CPL deliver expensive, low-volume leads. Authority framing isn't converting.
• Duplicate ad variants are cannibalizing each other with wildly different outcomes: two copies of 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' show €52.21 vs €143.79 CPL. Same name, one is 3x worse — audience overlap or fatigue is killing the weaker twin.
• 'General Video #1 - Copy' (€304 spend) hit €152.17 CPL — video duplication without creative iteration just burns budget.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more comparison statics with varied layouts, price points, and visual treatments — this angle has proven at both low and high spend. Test different home value tiers (€200K, €350K, €500K) to segment messaging.
• Invest in video content that mirrors the 'General Video #1' formula — direct, empowerment-led, showing the process. Layer in real seller testimonials for social proof.
• Create FR-language versions of every winning Vergelijking creative — Belgium is bilingual and you're likely under-serving Wallonia with NL-first assets.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the €143.79 CPL 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' immediately — €719 spent for 5 leads is unacceptable when the same concept runs at €43 CPL elsewhere.
• Kill 'Static _ De Tijd 2' — press authority angle isn't resonating at €60 CPL. Homeowners want savings math, not media clippings.
• Kill the €152.17 CPL 'General Video #1 - Copy' — two leads for €304. The original video works; this copy doesn't.

Belgium

27 ads · €1376 spend · 50 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Urgency and countdown framing is the clear winner: "Video _ Urgency #3" (21 purchases, 6.45x ROAS) and "Video _ Tickets Countdown #4" (16 purchases, 15.71x ROAS at €4.22 CPP) dominate conversions on a fraction of the top spend.
• Static key visuals convert efficiently at low spend: "Static _ Paradisco Key Visual #1" delivered 7.62x ROAS and "Static _ Urgency #6" hit 35.79x on minimal budget — suggesting static urgency formats deserve far more budget.
• Scarcity-driven copy crushes lineup-focused creative. The top 2 converters by volume are both urgency/countdown themed, proving this audience responds to FOMO over information.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Video _ Saturday Lineup #1" burned €530 for 1 purchase (0.1x ROAS) — the single biggest budget drain in the account. Lineup reveal content without urgency framing does not convert.
• Aftermovie content is a vanity play: "Video _ Aftermovie #1" spent €65 for 1 purchase at 0.78x ROAS. Nostalgia doesn't sell tickets.
• "Static _ Urgency #4" and "Video _ Friday Lineup #1" each spent €23-26 with zero purchases — dead weight sitting in the auction.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more countdown/scarcity video creatives — iterate on the "Tickets Countdown #4" format with different hooks, ticket-quantity callouts, and deadline framing.
• Scale urgency statics aggressively — "Static _ Urgency #6" and "Static _ Paradisco Key Visual #1" prove that simple, bold static urgency cards can outperform video on efficiency. Build a library of 5-8 variations.
• Test short-form FOMO reels: combine 3-5 second crowd/energy clips with hard urgency overlays (text counters, "X tickets left") to merge the emotional pull of aftermovies with the conversion power of countdown ads.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill "Video _ Saturday Lineup #1" immediately — €530 for 0.1x ROAS is unacceptable and Meta will keep spending on it.
• Kill all aftermovie creatives as direct-response ads. "Aftermovie #1" and "Aftermovie #2" have no conversion signal; repurpose them as organic content only.
• Kill "Video _ Friday Lineup #1" and "Static _ Urgency #4" — enough spend to prove they're not converting.

✅ What's Working
• Static offer creatives are the revenue engine: 'Static _ Offer #1 - Copy' is a unicorn at 12.74x ROAS and €39.45 CPP — the copy variant dramatically outperforms the original (2.17x), suggesting the iteration nailed better copy or audience.
• Renée UGC/testimonial video format converts: 'Video _ Renée #1 - Copy' delivers 4x ROAS at scale (€968 spend, 19 purchases) — proof that real-person endorsement beats polished studio content.
• Lifestyle statics quietly perform: 'Static _ Lifestyle #2 - Copy' at 2.29x ROAS with 116% CTR shows aspiration-driven imagery earns clicks and converts efficiently at €50.52 CPP.
❌ What's Not Working
• Ziris Split video format is a money pit: 'Video _ Ziris Split #1' burned €264 for 1 sale (0.55x ROAS) and 'Video _ Ziris Split #2' spent €82 with zero purchases — the split-screen concept isn't landing.
• Offer fatigue beyond #1: 'Static _ Offer #2' (1.28x), 'Offer #3' (0.92x), and 'Offer #4' (€63, zero purchases) all fail — only the original Offer #1 and its copy convert, suggesting the others have weaker hooks or less compelling deals.
• Polished video gets ignored: 'Video _ Studio #1' has the lowest CTR in the account (41.47%) — overproduced content repels this audience.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more static offer creatives iterating on the Offer #1 formula — test new copy angles, colorways, and urgency hooks while keeping the same visual framework that drove 12.74x ROAS.
• Scale the Renée UGC playbook: recruit 2-3 more Belgian cyclists/runners for testimonial-style videos — the format is proven at 4x ROAS and the account desperately needs more winning video creative.
• Lean into lifestyle statics showing real riding/running scenarios with product visible — the 'Lifestyle #2 - Copy' performance suggests authenticity + aspiration beats product-on-white catalog shots.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Ziris Split videos immediately — three variants, €452 combined spend, 1 total purchase. The format is dead.
• Kill Offer variants #2, #3, #4 — they've had enough spend to prove they don't convert. Stop subsidizing losers while the #1 copy variant prints money.
• Stop making polished studio content — 'Video _ Studio #1' confirms this audience wants real-world and UGC, not brand films.

OR Coffee — Ads Report

5 August 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads + Klaviyo Email · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

10 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

10 ads · €2927 spend · 112 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Catalog carousels are crushing it — "Catalog Carousel - Specialty Coffee" (68.24x ROAS, €7.68 CPP) and "Catalog Carousel - Espresso Coffee" (19.78x ROAS, 59 purchases) are the engine. Product-level dynamic creative + high intent = money printer.
• Retargeting/lifecycle statics are absurdly efficient — "Static _ Repeat #1" (79.28x ROAS, €4.32 CPP) and "Static _ Hold #2" (7.4x ROAS, €10.60 CPP) prove that warm audiences convert at pennies. These are barely spending but printing.
• Origin and product-focused statics deliver strong ROAS at low spend — "Static _ Origin #1" (14.2x ROAS) shows the specialty/origin story angle resonates with this audience.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Video _ OR Coffee" is the highest spend ad (€1,221) but only 9 purchases at €135.66 CPP and 4.45x ROAS — it's eating budget that catalog and statics would use 10x better. Brand video without clear product/conversion intent is leaking money.
• "Carousel__Filter - Copy" is underperforming at 3.59x ROAS and €42.93 CPP with only 6 purchases — the filter angle isn't converting efficiently and the "Copy" suffix suggests a lazy duplicate, not a real iteration.
• "Static_Barista_Courses - Copy" (5.79x ROAS, 2 purchases, €43.92 CPP) — promoting courses in an e-commerce conversion campaign is a distraction. Wrong objective for this creative.
⬆ Double Down On
• Catalog carousels segmented by use case or collection — espresso, filter, single origin, subscriptions. The format is proven; create more variants with different entry points and product sets.
• Lifecycle/segment-specific statics (Repeat, Hold, Never) — these audiences are barely being spent on but convert insanely well. Build a full creative suite per funnel stage with tailored messaging.
• Origin story statics with product tie-in — "Static _ Origin #1" shows the specialty angle works. Produce a series: one per origin country, each anchored to a specific SKU with price and CTA.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop letting "Video _ OR Coffee" eat 40%+ of spend at €135 CPP. It's brand fluff in a performance campaign. Pause or hard-cap immediately.
• Kill the barista courses creative in e-commerce campaigns — it's off-objective and diluting ROAS.
• Stop duplicating ads with "- Copy" suffix and no real hypothesis. "Carousel__Filter - Copy" is lazy iteration, not testing.

Creative Analysis

6 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

6 ads · €131 spend · 0 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Comparison-angle creatives ("Thuis vs Publiek" series) earn the most algorithmic spend, with variant 03 absorbing 65% of budget at a strong 119.89% CTR — the home-vs-public framing clearly resonates with Belgian EV considerers.
• Educational/article-style content ("Static _ Artikel _ 01") delivers the second-highest CTR at 192.53% on €34 spend — informational positioning builds trust in a high-consideration category.
• "Static _ Thuisladen _ 03" posts the highest CTR of all (259.74%) despite minimal spend — pure home-charging messaging has untapped potential.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero purchases across every single ad despite €130+ total spend — the funnel is broken post-click. Either the landing page, offer, or conversion event is failing to close.
• "Static _ Thuis vs Publiek _ 01" has a dismal 40.49% CTR vs its siblings (119-214%) — that specific creative execution is dead weight within the winning angle.
• "Static _ Artikel _ 02" received zero delivery and zero engagement — Meta's system rejected it before it even competed.
⬆ Double Down On
• Home vs. public cost-savings comparisons with specific Belgian electricity pricing or per-kWh math — the comparison angle wins attention, now make it convert with concrete numbers.
• Article-style educational creatives that address Belgian-specific objections: installation permits, syndic approval for apartments, and subsidies/premiums (e.g., Flemish premie).
• Video or carousel walkthroughs of real Belgian installations (residential driveways, SME parking lots) — static-only is limiting trust-building for a €1,000+ product.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running static-only creative — zero purchases across six statics proves the format alone cannot close a high-ticket infrastructure sale.
• Kill "Static _ Thuis vs Publiek _ 01" and "Static _ Artikel _ 02" immediately — one underperforms its own angle by 3-5x, the other is DOA.
• Stop optimizing for purchase if the pixel has zero conversion data — switch to lead-gen (quote request) to feed the algorithm real signals.

• Dual-angle messaging: pair the investment USP (100% rental guarantee) with tangible lifestyle proof (actual property visuals, nature, dike village atmosphere) so clicks convert into qualified leads.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the all-investment, all-static monoculture — it generates curiosity clicks that go nowhere.
• Kill "Static _ Investeren _ 4" immediately — zero signal, zero potential.
• Stop running conversion-less creatives past €200 without iterating on the landing experience or creative CTA.

✅ What's Working
• Bauhaus creative theme earns the most algorithmic confidence — 6 variants getting spend with Bauhaus #5 (€562) and #6 (€77) showing the highest relative CTRs (628% and 545%), suggesting the Bauhaus aesthetic resonates with the target audience.
• The architectural-reference naming convention (Bauhaus, Naoshima, Sommerfeld) indicates strong brand-world creative — the design-led identity is clearly communicated, generating high engagement signals across all 12 ads.
• Meta is distributing spend decisively: top 3 ads capture 85% of budget, meaning the algorithm sees clear engagement winners — Bauhaus #5, Naoshima #2 (530% CTR), and Sommerfeld #3 (412% CTR).
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero conversions across all 12 ads on €1,632 total spend is a systemic failure — this is not a creative problem alone; the conversion event (purchase) is almost certainly misconfigured for a lead-gen real estate funnel. Nobody 'purchases' a €500K+ property via Meta pixel.
• All 12 creatives are static images — no video, no carousel, no motion. For luxury coastal architecture, this is a catastrophic missed opportunity. Static cannot convey spatial experience, light, or lifestyle.
• High-spend ads like Bauhaus #5 (€562), Naoshima #2 (€438), and Sommerfeld #3 (€387) are burning budget with zero downstream signal — engagement without conversion means people click, enjoy the design porn, and leave with no reason to inquire.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce cinematic video content: drone coastal shots, architectural walkthroughs, golden-hour interiors. This audience buys emotion and aspiration — static photos of modernist facades are table stakes, not closers.
• Build lead-form-native ads with a clear value exchange: 'Request the Rietveld brochure,' 'Book a private visit,' 'See available penthouses.' Current ads appear to lack any conversion mechanism beyond a click.
• Lean into the family-founder story and the 'passion over profit-per-sqm' USP — this differentiates RRR from every other Belgian coast developer. One strong founder-narrative video could outperform all 12 current statics combined.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the purchase-based conversion objective immediately — switch to lead generation (instant forms) or at minimum optimize for on-site lead events. Every euro spent optimizing for 'purchase' on luxury real estate is an euro wasted.
• Stop running 12 static variants simultaneously with no conversion tracking fix — you're A/B testing creative while the funnel has no floor. Fix the plumbing before testing the paint.
• Pause all three top-spend ads (Bauhaus #5, Naoshima #2, Sommerfeld #3) until conversion tracking is corrected — they've proven they can generate clicks, not leads.

Belgium

30 ads · €2357 spend · 0 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Moment-based B2B framing wins — "Static _ B2B _ 4 Momenten #1" combines strong spend (€290) with top-tier CTR (191.98%), proving 'show when to sell' beats 'just stock it'.
• Objection-busting and benefit-led angles generate disproportionate engagement — "Static _ B2B _ Geen excuus #1" (CTR 203.87%) and "Static _ B2B _ Boost #2" (CTR 144.05%) outperform generic B2B pitches.
• B2C concepts are exploding with minimal spend — "Static _ Pronounce #1" (CTR 451.25%, €5), "Static _ Bowl #2" (CTR 253.78%, €35), and "Static _ Nutri A #2" (CTR 195.94%, €124) are the account's best engagement rates but get almost no budget.
❌ What's Not Working
• Biggest spenders are mediocre — "Static _ B2B _ Açai Koffiebar" eats €513 at CTR 118% and "Static _ B2B _ Upgrade Brunch" burns €309 at CTR 95.92%; generic B2B positioning soaks up budget without earning proportionate engagement.
• Operational messaging is dead weight — both "Snel" variants (CTR ~91%) and both "Menukaart" variants (CTR 0–95%) cluster at the bottom; 'quick' and 'menu card' angles do not differentiate.
• Video is functionally untested — €9 total across two creatives; "Video _ Organic _ Soft Serve" flopped (CTR 19.96%) while "Video _ Functional Drinks 4" (CTR 385.46%) never got a chance at €4 spend.
⬆ Double Down On
• Flood B2C with real budget — 70% of spend goes to B2B but your stated target is consumers 18–35; "Pronounce", "Bowl", and "Nutri A" concepts are screaming for investment and map directly to quality/nutrition USPs.
• Scale the objection-busting framework into consumer-facing creative — "Geen excuus" works for B2B; build B2C equivalents addressing price perception, prep complexity, and 'where to buy' friction at Bio-Planet/Delhaize.
• Build a video pipeline immediately — you have zero tested video at scale for a deeply visual, story-rich product; endorser content (Bekkari, Gruyaert, Dr. Binge) and sourcing stories are obvious formats sitting unused.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All "Snel" and "Menukaart" variants — four ads, €327 combined spend, consistently the worst CTRs in the B2B set. The concepts are generic and unredeemable.
• "Static _ B2B _ This is how we bowl" — CTR 68.70% is the lowest among funded ads; the English-language pun doesn't land in a Dutch/French market.
• "Video _ Organic _ Soft Serve" — worst CTR in the entire account (19.96%); a repurposed organic clip isn't a paid creative strategy.

✅ What's Working
• Both ads generate absurdly high CTRs (126%+ and 99%+), meaning the creative hooks are grabbing attention effectively. The ad format likely drives engagement through carousels or interactive elements.
• The brand is getting cheap clicks in the Belgian B2B workwear niche — there is clear audience interest at the top of funnel.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero purchases across both ads despite €90 total spend. 120239393986810631 burned €86 with nothing to show — the funnel is broken post-click.
• Sky-high CTR paired with zero conversions screams landing page disconnect or wrong conversion objective. Clicks are meaningless if nobody buys.
• 120239394435940631 got only €4 in spend — either budget allocation is broken or Meta's algorithm already deprioritized it due to poor signals.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the post-click experience first: no creative will save a broken landing page. Align offer, language, and CTA from ad to checkout.
• Lean into direct-response creative with clear B2B offers (free quote, bulk pricing, sample requests) instead of awareness-style engagement bait.
• Test lead generation objectives (Meta lead forms) to capture intent without relying on a potentially broken website funnel.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running purchase-optimized campaigns until the landing page and conversion tracking are verified and functional.
• Kill vanity CTR as a success metric — it is masking a complete conversion failure.

Belgium

24 ads · €1756 spend · 4 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Video format is the only format converting — "Video _ Call #2 - Copy" (3 purch, €116 CPP) and "Video _ DM #1 - Copy" (1 purch, €86 CPP) are the only ads with purchases.
• Call-to-action themes around booking a call or sending a DM create enough intent to drive purchases — static ads with the same themes generate zero.
❌ What's Not Working
• Every single static ad has zero purchases — 16 static creatives, €920+ in combined spend, not one conversion. "Static _ Matthias #1" burned €359 alone with nothing to show.
• Broad business-angle statics ("Static _ Business #1 - Copy" at €148, "Static _ Business #3" at €70) are generic and non-converting — no clear CTA or differentiation.
• "Video _ DM #2 - Copy" spent €318 with zero purchases despite being a video — suggesting the specific creative or hook in version #2 fails to close.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more video creatives with direct CTA hooks (book a call, send a DM) — the only two converting formats both use this pattern.
• Create video testimonials featuring real users (Matthias, Gunther, Anthony) — their static versions drove high CTR but zero conversions, video could close the gap.
• Build video creatives with concrete before/after results and social proof — combine the "Review" and "BefoAfter" angles in video format since static versions died.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all static ads immediately. 16 statics, €920 spent, zero purchases. The format is dead in this market for this offer.
• Kill "Video _ DM #2 - Copy" — €318 spent, zero purchases. Something in that specific creative repels buyers despite the DM angle working in version #1.
• Stop spreading budget across 20 ads. Concentrate on the 2 converters and new video tests.

🌐

Other

30 ads · €8763 spend · 0 purchases
✅ What's Working
• High engagement on native and animation formats — Brugge_penthouse (375% CTR), Blom_apt_native (306% CTR), and Vottem_animatie (209% CTR) prove aspirational visuals and motion grab attention.
• Slideshow formats deliver solid engagement across projects — georges_slideshow (168% CTR) and wildebeek_slideshow_realisatie_variaties (104% CTR) show multi-image storytelling resonates.
• Terrace/exterior lifestyle angles outperform interiors — west_terras_cta (160% CTR), stokerie_terras (142% CTR) signal outdoor living is a hook.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero purchases across ALL 20 ads on €7,461 total spend — this is a catastrophic funnel failure, not just a creative problem. Tracking, landing pages, or conversion objective is broken.
• CTA-heavy static images underperform on engagement AND convert nothing — Charleroi-image-cta v2 (57% CTR), georges_image_CTA_v1 (67% CTR) are the weakest engagement with zero return.
• Budget is atomized across 9+ projects with no winner emerging — spreading €300-700 per project prevents any single funnel from reaching statistical significance.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the funnel FIRST — audit pixel firing, landing page load times, and conversion event setup before spending another euro. Engagement without conversion means the bottom of funnel is broken.
• Consolidate budget behind 2-3 top projects and run lead gen objective ads with in-platform forms to bypass potential landing page failures.
• Lean into the high-CTR formats — native placements, animation/motion, and terrace/lifestyle exterior angles — but pair them with clear qualification copy to attract buyers, not browsers.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running conversion-optimized campaigns until tracking is verified — €7,461 with zero purchases means Meta's algorithm has no conversion signal to optimize toward.
• Kill the low-CTR CTA image variants (Charleroi-image-cta v2, georges_image_cta_v1_rem, wildebeek_flexibele units) — they're boring creatively and delivering nothing.
• Stop splitting budget across 9 projects simultaneously — consolidate or kill the weakest-performing project funnels entirely.

Belgium

24 ads · €3013 spend · 0 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Extremely high CTRs across the board — "Static _ Doorstromer #1" at 370% CTR and "Static _ Algemeen #1" at 296% CTR show the static creative is generating massive click engagement.
• "Doorstromer" audience segment is attracting the most spend allocation (€527 + €462 top two), suggesting Meta's algorithm sees signal there.
• Segmented messaging by life stage (Alleenstaand, Doorstromer, Jong Koppel, Algemeen) is a smart structure — it's generating broad click interest across all segments.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero purchases across ALL 20 ads with €2,979 total spend — this is a catastrophic post-click conversion failure. Every euro is wasted until the funnel is fixed.
• CTRs above 100% are almost certainly inflated by link clicks vs. outbound clicks, or misconfigured tracking — real engagement is unknowable, making optimization blind.
• Duplicated ads ("- Copy" variants) like "Static _ Doorstromer #1 - Copy" and "Static _ Jong Koppel #2 - Copy" add spend fragmentation without any conversion learning.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the landing page and tracking BEFORE any new creative spend — zero purchases on nearly €3K means the site or pixel is broken, not the ads.
• Once the funnel is fixed, lean into the Doorstromer segment — it's absorbing the most spend and clicks, suggesting strongest audience resonance.
• Introduce video and UGC formats — all 20 ads are static, and there's zero format diversity to test whether motion improves conversion rates.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all "- Copy" duplicates immediately — they serve no strategic purpose and split budget away from originals with no conversion data to justify them.
• Stop running any ad until you've verified pixel fires, confirmed the purchase event triggers correctly, and validated the landing page loads and converts. €2,979 with 0 purchases is unacceptable.

🛑 Kill or Rethink

🌐

Other

4 ads · €170 spend · 0 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Extremely high CTRs across all ads suggest creative is grabbing attention — people are curious about carports, pergolas, and verandas.
• Product category diversification (carports, pergolas, verandas, PVC) is smart for a multi-service business — tests breadth of demand.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero purchases across every single ad despite €170 total spend — the funnel is completely broken post-click. Landing page, offer, or conversion tracking is the bottleneck, not the creative.
• All campaigns are set to 'conversion' objective but selling high-ticket home improvements (€5K-€30K+) directly via purchase event is unrealistic — these are lead-gen products, not e-commerce.
• Budgets are spread paper-thin (€5-€84) across 4 ads — none had enough spend to exit learning phase or generate meaningful data.
⬆ Double Down On
• Switch entirely to lead generation (instant forms or landing page with quote request) — nobody buys a veranda via an add-to-cart button.
• Produce project showcase content: completed installations with before/after, drone shots, happy homeowners — build trust for a high-ticket decision.
• Lean into local proof: reference Colmar and Liège specifically in headlines and visuals to trigger local relevance and trust.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running purchase-optimized campaigns for products that require consultations and quotes — it guarantees zero tracked conversions.
• Stop splitting tiny budgets across 4 campaigns — consolidate into 1-2 campaigns with proper budget to exit learning phase.

✅ What's Working
• Absolutely nothing is converting — €6,909 total spend, zero purchases across all 20 ads. This account is bleeding money.
• Video formats (VERANDA VERANCOBEL - VIDEO, PVCS_VIDEO_MUTLI3) generate highest engagement rates, suggesting creative resonance exists but the funnel is completely broken.
• Verancobel-branded ads (PERGOLA VERANCOBEL, PVC VERANCOBEL) show stronger engagement than generic product ads, indicating brand equity has pull.
❌ What's Not Working
• The entire conversion strategy is broken — pergolas, carports, and verandas are €5,000-€30,000+ products. Nobody 'purchases' these through a Meta ad. You're optimizing for the wrong event.
• PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_MUTLI4 burned €2,465 across three variants with zero results. CARPORTS burned €2,014 across three variants — same story. This is reckless spend without conversion validation.
• Ad naming ('Copie', 'MUTLI' typos, duplicate names) reveals a disorganized multi-account with no testing discipline and likely no proper attribution setup.
⬆ Double Down On
• Switch ALL campaigns to Lead Generation objective with instant forms — collect quote requests, not purchases. These are high-ticket home improvement products.
• Video-first creative featuring real Verancobel installations — the two video ads show 2x+ engagement vs. static. Build a video pipeline.
• Localized social proof content — before/after projects, customer testimonials, installation time-lapses. Trust is everything for €10K+ home purchases.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill every single purchase-optimized campaign immediately. You've spent €6,909 proving the purchase event doesn't work for this product category.
• Kill duplicate ad proliferation — three identical CARPORTS ads and three PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_MUTLI4 ads competing against each other is auction self-cannibalization.
• Kill the 'multi compte' shared account structure until you verify proper pixel/CAPI setup per product line. This account has zero conversion infrastructure.

5 ads · €990 spend · 0 purchases
✅ What's Working
• The two 'Algemeen' creatives (Visual and GIF) show astronomical CTRs (274% and 263%), signaling the broad provincial branding hook resonates far more than location-specific angles.
• Influencer-led creative for specific domains works unevenly — 'Magnolia - Phof' pulls a strong 71% CTR at €228 spend, proving the right creator × right location is a winning formula.
• The IZWVL campaign structure (general brand + creator × domain pairings) is sound for a public-sector awareness play.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Chloe - Bulskampveld' underperforms at 30.78% CTR — lowest engagement of the set at meaningful spend (€228). The creator or the domain angle isn't landing.
• 'Algemeen - GIF' received only €6 despite a 263% CTR — Meta barely delivered it, suggesting audience overlap issues or a broken ad-set setup throttling the best-performing format.
• 'TheLifePlanFamily - Palingbeek' got just €74 spend with a mediocre 37.85% CTR — neither the algorithm nor the audience loved it.
⬆ Double Down On
• General provincial branding creatives: the 'Algemeen' approach massively outperforms location-specific ads on engagement — produce more variations (carousel, Reels, cinemagraph).
• High-engagement creator pairings like 'Magnolia - Phof': replicate this model with new creators at other provincial domains (Raversyde, De Gavers, etc.).
• Animated/motion formats: the GIF's CTR rivals the static visual despite near-zero spend — invest properly in motion-first creative across all domain campaigns.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop spending on 'Chloe - Bulskampveld' — at €228 and 30.78% CTR it's the weakest creator pairing by a wide margin. Replace the creator or rethink the Bulskampveld angle.
• Don't let 'TheLifePlanFamily - Palingbeek' limp along at €74 — either give it a proper test budget or cut it entirely.
• Stop running the GIF at €6 — fix the delivery issue or consolidate it into a working ad set. A €6 'test' tells you nothing.

Belgium

15 ads · €490 spend · 70 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Video Story format is the undisputed winner — "Video _ Story #1" delivers 38.7x ROAS at €2.55 CPP, and "Video _ Story #3" hits 16.41x ROAS. Narrative video sells tickets.
• Static formats pull weight at both ends — "Static _ Key Visual #1" is the reliable workhorse absorbing €194 at 7.17x ROAS, while "Static _ Cover #1" quietly crushes at 33.26x ROAS on just €14 spend.
• Ticket-update urgency framing converts in video — "Video _ Ticket Update #1" (€62) hits 14.47x ROAS proving scarcity copy works when wrapped in engaging video.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video Key Visual format is dead on arrival — "Video _ Key Visual #1" burned €34 with zero purchases; the key visual concept works as static but collapses as video.
• "Video _ Last 250 #1" wasted €34 with zero conversions — scarcity headline alone without storytelling or proof doesn't move tickets.
• Too many low-spend creatives (six ads under €5) sitting in data purgatory, cluttering the account and splitting learnings.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Video Story variations — this is the highest-ROAS format by a wide margin. Test new angles: lineup teasers, behind-the-scenes, attendee hype.
• Scale "Static _ Cover #1" immediately — 33.26x ROAS at €14 spend is criminally underfunded. Give it real budget.
• Lean into ticket-urgency messaging paired with video storytelling — combine the scarcity angle of Ticket Update with the narrative power of the Story format.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause "Video _ Key Visual #1" and "Video _ Last 250 #1" now — €68 combined spend, zero purchases, zero signal. They're dead.
• Stop splitting budget across low-spend duplicates. Consolidate "Video _ Story #2" and "Video _ Ticket Update #1" variants into single ad sets to exit learning phase faster.

• Reel Marie Jo Lisbeth' broke the Reel pattern with €49 spent and 0 purchases — product or creator mismatch killed it.
• Event-based and store-visit ads like 'Evenement: Fête des Belges' are not driving measurable online conversions at all.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more creator Reels modeled after Merlene's format — she outperformed everything by 10x+. Clone that structure with new creators and products immediately.
• Lean into personality-first content where creators demonstrate or style the product on camera. The data is screaming: faces sell, flat-lay graphics don't.
• Test scaling Reel winners with incremental budget increases before launching new static concepts. The €23→22.52x ROAS signal on Merlene is begging for more spend.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all static 'Bericht' sale announcements. Nine of them ran, zero converted. The format is dead for this account.
• Stop boosting event/store-visit posts for online purchase objectives — 'Fête des Belges' and 'Deze week kan je hier terecht' are wrong objective for wrong format.
